title: Audit types declared by crate lakekeeper

action_name.description: The action's wire name, from a vocabulary enum of any emitter.

ActionRecord.description: An `action` object: the wire name and the action's context fields.

principal.description: The authenticated principal. Present for `principal` and `assumed-role`.

assumed_role.description: The role acted as. Present for `assumed-role`; `principal` is still the human.

ActorRecord.description: The `actor` object: who made the request, as authentication established it.

gate.description: The gate that rejected the request.

denied_by.description: The rule of the gate that decided, when the gate names one.

status.description: The HTTP status the caller received.

error_type.description: The error type the caller received.

message.description:
The gate's own wording. Suppressing the error-response line takes this
with it, and it is what separates two rejections that share a type —
a gate failing closed on a missing precondition from the same gate
failing closed on an unreachable upstream.

error_id.description: The id the caller can quote to correlate with this record.

request_id.description:
The request this rejection belongs to, repeated out of the span so the record stands
alone.

AdmissionRejectedContext.description:
Context for the admission-rejection audit record: which gate refused the request, on what
grounds, and what the caller was told.

`error_id` is the id the caller was handed, so a user's report resolves to this record.
`request_id` is repeated out of the span, so the record stands alone.

role_id.description: The role's id in this catalog.

provider_id.description: The provider that supplied the role.

source_id.description: The role's id at the provider.

AssumedRoleRecord.description: The role an `assumed-role` actor acts as.

x-audit-descriptions.forbidden: An admission gate denied the caller authoritatively.
x-audit-descriptions.unavailable:
An admission gate could not reach an upstream it needs and failed closed.
Separate from `forbidden` so an outage of that upstream reads as an outage
rather than as a wave of denials.

x-audit-descriptions.ActionForbidden: Action is not allowed for the user
x-audit-descriptions.CannotSeeResource: Resource exists but user lacks permission to see it
x-audit-descriptions.InternalCatalogError: An internal Catalog error occurred before authorization check could be completed
x-audit-descriptions.InvalidRequestData: Invalid data provided by the client that caused authorization to fail (e.g. malformed resource identifier)

emitter.description: Which product produced this record, and the version of what it governs.

actions.description: The actions evaluated, always a list however many there are.

entities.description: The entities they were evaluated against, always a list.

actor.description: Who made the request, as authentication established it.

privilege_source.description: Which authority answered: the authorizer, or a bypass.

user_agent.description: The `User-Agent` header, verbatim and unverified. Absent when none was sent.

break_glass.description: The stated break-glass reason. Absent unless the caller claimed one.

context.description: Handler-supplied detail about the request. Absent when the handler added none.

idempotency_key.description: The request's `Idempotency-Key`. Absent when the caller sent none.

failure_reason.description: Why a denied record was denied, as the vocabulary spells it.

error.description: The error the caller received. Present only on a denial that produced one.

AuthorizationRecord.description: An authorization record: was this caller permitted to do these actions on these entities?

x-audit-descriptions.manage_tags: Attach/detach governance tags on this generic table.
x-audit-descriptions.read_grants: Can list the grants held on this generic table.

x-audit-descriptions.accept_moved_namespace:
Accept a namespace being moved in from elsewhere as a child of this entity.

Distinct from `CreateNamespace`: creating adds an *empty* child, so exposing it to
this subtree's grantees exposes nothing. A move arrives carrying existing contents
and their direct grants, which is why this is gated on grant authority in addition to
`create` — without it, a namespace could be populated and granted somewhere
permissive and then moved into a `managed_access` subtree, smuggling grants past the
control that subtree exists to enforce.
x-audit-descriptions.manage_tags: Attach/detach governance tags on this namespace.
x-audit-descriptions.move:
Move this namespace to a new path, re-parenting and/or renaming it.

Gated on grant-level authority *in addition to* plain write access. Re-parenting a
namespace re-issues every privilege the destination subtree confers onto the
namespace's contents, with no assignment record anywhere — so the actor must
already be able to grant on the namespace being moved. Inside a `managed_access`
subtree ownership does not confer that, which is precisely the case where moving
out would otherwise defeat the control.

Only the source half of a move's authorization; the destination is gated by
`CreateNamespace` plus `AcceptMovedNamespace`.
x-audit-descriptions.read_grants: Can list the grants held on this namespace.
x-audit-descriptions.read_subtree_grants:
Can list and read every grant in the subtree rooted here: the namespace's own and
those on every descendant namespace and tabular. Strictly stronger than
`ReadGrants`, which covers this one resource; granted separately because it
enumerates the subtree.

`scope` states what the listing covers — the resource kinds it reaches, how far its
range extends, the privileges it covers, and the principal it is narrowed to — so a
policy can allow a narrow access review and still refuse a full enumeration.

Every enforced check carries it: Lakekeeper authorizes a real subtree listing or
revoke only with a scope. An absent scope is the base-capability question that
permission introspection asks, so an authorizer may answer the two separately —
refusing the base question drops the action from
`GET /{warehouse,namespace}/{id}/actions` and leaves real calls untouched.
x-audit-descriptions.revoke_subtree_grants:
Can revoke any grant in the subtree rooted here, asked once at this namespace for
the whole batch. An authorizer must answer it as authority over everything
beneath — or refuse the subtree routes.

`scope` states what the revoke covers, on the same terms as `ReadSubtreeGrants`.

x-audit-descriptions.create_tag: Create a new governance tag definition in this project.
x-audit-descriptions.list_tags: List tag definitions in this project.
x-audit-descriptions.read_grants: Can list the grants held on this project.

x-audit-descriptions.manage_role_assignments: Can add/remove members (user or role) of this role.
x-audit-descriptions.read_role_assignments: Can list members / parents / assignments of this role.
x-audit-descriptions.update_source_system:
Can rebind this role's external identity (provider + source id) to a
different source system. `target` is the rebind destination, surfaced as
action context (`requested_provider_id` / `requested_source_id`) so policy-based
authorizers can gate it (e.g. forbid moving a role onto a particular
provider). The catalog backend treats this the same as
`ManageRoleAssignments`.

The destination is explicit. A real rebind names the target provider and source id;
the permission enumeration behind `GET /role/{id}/actions`, and any "may this
principal rebind at all?" query, name `any` instead. `any` is a base-capability
marker, not a permissive default: a policy written against a concrete destination
gates that destination and never matches `any`, and a `/check` caller picks between
the two deliberately.

x-audit-descriptions.apply: Attach this tag to a target. Also requires `manage_tags` on the target.
x-audit-descriptions.read: Read the tag definition (name, description, value kind, allowed values).
x-audit-descriptions.read_attachments:
List the targets this tag is attached to (reverse lookup). Broader disclosure
than `Read`, so restricted to tag owners / project security admins. Distinct
from `can_read_assignments`, which reads who holds apply/ownership (grants).
x-audit-descriptions.read_grants: Can list the grants held on this tag definition.
x-audit-descriptions.remove: Detach this tag from a target. Also requires `manage_tags` on the target.
x-audit-descriptions.update: Update the tag definition (name/description, widen scope, add allowed values).

anyOf.description: A set of key-value pairs (e.g. properties, `updated_properties`).
A single string value (e.g. resource name, ID).

id.description: The client's id for this check in a batch, or its index. Absent for single checks.

for-principal.description: The principal whose permission was evaluated, when it is not the request's actor.

entity.description: The entity the action was evaluated against.

allowed.description: The authorizer's answer. Absent when an upstream error stopped the evaluation.

determined_by.description:
The policies or rules that determined the decision, when the authorizer reports them.
The same shape the management API returns for a check, so one parser reads both.

DecisionRecord.description:
One entry of `authorizations[]`: which action on which entity was evaluated, for whom,
with what result.

policy-id.description:
Stable, authorizer-assigned identifier of the policy (e.g. the Cedar
`PolicyId`). Always present.

name.description:
Human-facing name the author gave the policy (e.g. a `@name` or
`@id` annotation). Neither required nor guaranteed unique; absent
when the author provided none.

effect.description: Whether the policy permits or forbids.

source.description:
Opaque origin of the policy (e.g. a policy-source identifier).
Absent when the authorizer cannot attribute a source.

oneOf.description:
A policy that determined the decision, surfaced by a policy-based
authorizer.

source.description:
Opaque, authorizer-assigned identifier of the built-in authority
tier that granted the action. Absent when none can be attributed.

reason.description:
Human-facing reason the tier applied (e.g. an administrator
lockout-recovery grant). Absent when the authorizer gives none.

oneOf.description:
An allow contributed by a built-in/system authority tier that takes
precedence over normal authored policy — e.g. a recovery mechanism that
lets a privileged system role act despite a policy that would otherwise
forbid it. Its presence means the verdict rested on built-in authority
rather than on a configured policy.

DeterminingFactor.description:
A single factor that contributed to an authorization decision.

Discriminated by `type`: `policy` names a policy the authorizer matched, and
`system-authority` records that a built-in authority tier decided the request. The
schema is a closed `oneOf` over those two, so a further kind is a schema change a
generated client has to be rebuilt for rather than one it absorbs on its own.

name.description: The emitter's name, unique across the products that write to this log.

format.description: The `MAJOR.MINOR` version of what this emitter contributes.

EmitterRecord.description:
The `emitter` object: which product produced this record, and the version of the
vocabulary and context shapes it governs.

A consumer routes the core shape on `audit_format` and everything the emitter owns — its
`context`, its vocabulary, any shape it defines — on this.

EntityRecord.description: An `entity` object: the kind of resource and its identifying fields.

type.description: The error type the caller received.

code.description: The HTTP status the caller received.

message.description: The error message the caller received.

stack.description: The error's stack of causes, innermost first. Absent when empty.

error_id.description: The id the caller can quote to correlate with this record.

ErrorRecord.description: The `error` object of a denied authorization record.

privilege.description: The privilege name, verbatim from the authorizer's vocabulary.

resource_type.description: The kind of resource the grant is on.

resource_id.description: The exact resource. Absent for server grants, whose type is their whole identity.

warehouse_id.description: The containing warehouse, for warehouse-scoped resources.

GrantContextRecord.description:
The `context` of a grant record: the full `(principal, privilege, resource)` triple. Grants
are hard-deleted and keep no history, so a revocation's triple exists nowhere else once the
row is gone.

HandlerContext.description: The `context` map of an authorization record: keys a handler recorded, with string values.

x-audit-descriptions.entity_id: The id of the entity a task operation addressed.
x-audit-descriptions.invoked-by: Which operation invoked this one, when a handler acts on behalf of another.
x-audit-descriptions.queue_name: The task queue an operation addressed.
x-audit-descriptions.self-provisioning: Whether the user creation was the caller provisioning itself.
x-audit-descriptions.self-read: Whether a grant read asked about the caller's own grants.

x-audit-descriptions.set_warehouse_managed_by: Set or clear a warehouse's managed-by marker.

emitter.description: Which product produced this record, and the version of what it governs.

operation.description: What was done, from the emitter's own vocabulary.

actor.description: Who made the request, as authentication established it.

outcome.description: How it ended, from the emitter's own vocabulary.

context.description:
The operation's own detail. One shape per operation kind, each declared by its
emitter; absent for an operation that carries none.

OperationRecord.description:
An operation record: something the system did that touches identity or access, with no
permission decision of its own. Any emitter can produce one.

PolicyEffect.description: Whether a determining policy permits or forbids.

x-audit-descriptions.authorizer: Decision came from the configured authorizer (OpenFGA, Cedar, `AllowAll`, ...).
x-audit-descriptions.instance_admin:
Principal listed in `LAKEKEEPER__INSTANCE_ADMINS`. Control-plane bypass
only; data-plane actions still route through the configured authorizer.
x-audit-descriptions.internal:
A call the catalog made to itself, with no client request behind it. Full bypass,
including data-plane actions.

x-audit-descriptions.authorization: Was this caller permitted to do these actions on these entities?
x-audit-descriptions.operation: Something the system did that touches identity or access.
x-audit-descriptions.replay: A retry answered from an idempotency record, so no authorization ran.

emitter.description: Which product produced this record, and the version of what it governs.

actions.description: The actions the replayed request named, always a list.

entities.description:
The entities it named, always a list. As the caller wrote them: a replay resolves
nothing.

actor.description: Who made the request, as authentication established it.

privilege_source.description: Which authority would have answered, had one been asked.

user_agent.description: The `User-Agent` header, verbatim and unverified. Absent when none was sent.

idempotency_key.description:
The key whose stored response was served. Always present: it is what makes this a
replay.

ReplayRecord.description: A replay record: a retry answered from an idempotency record, so no authorization ran.

x-audit-descriptions.tag-definition:
Spelled `tag-definition` on the wire, matching the path segment tag definitions
are addressed by, so every key of the vocabulary map names its own URL segment.
The only spelling `kebab-case` does not already produce.

RoleSubjectRecord.description: A role named as a target.

x-audit-descriptions.excluded: Only grants held below the addressed resource are in range.
x-audit-descriptions.included:
The request's range extends to the addressed resource itself. The kinds it
actually reaches are in `resource_types`; a kind filter can still exclude the
root's own kind.

SubjectRecord.description:
A principal named as a target: `for-principal` on a decision entry, `principal` on a grant
record. `{"user": …}` or `{"role": …}`.

UserSubjectRecord.description: A user named as a target.
